title: skills.json
description: A portable, verifiable inventory of agent-executable skills. Discoverable at /.well-known/skills.json or in a repository's top-level .skills/ directory.

id.description: Stable identity. A domain the subject controls, so the profile is self-hosted rather than platform-held.

kind.description: Humans and agents publish the same document. That is the point.

model.description: For kind=agent: the model the skills were authored against and are claimed to work on.

path.description: Path to the SKILL.md, relative to skills.json.

digest.description: Content hash of SKILL.md. A receipt is bound to a digest, so editing a skill invalidates its receipts. This is what stops a verified skill being quietly swapped for a different one.

kind.description: diagnostic: recognise a misleading symptom. constraint: a hard rule of some system. procedure: a sequence to follow. recipe: a reusable implementation.

domains.description: Technologies the skill applies to. The search index, and the input to staleness.

requires.description: Skill names this one composes with. These are the edges of the graph -- the honest replacement for connections.

discovered_in.description: The project where the lesson was actually paid for.

evidence.description: A PR, commit, incident or log the claim can be chased to.

assurance.description: The whole reason this format exists. Separates what has been proven from what is merely asserted.

level.description: asserted: written down, nothing more. field-observed: the fix was seen to work in production, but not reproducibly. self-verified: an eval case runs and passes on the author's own machine. notarised: a third party ran the eval and signed the result. Only the last is a credential; the first is a LinkedIn skill.

verified_against.description: The exact version, model or service the claim was checked against. Absent means the claim floats.

stale_after_days.description: How long a verification stays meaningful for this domain. A pinned library constraint ages slowly; a hosted-API behaviour ages fast.

runnable.description: false means the case is written but needs a harness or credentials to execute. An honest profile says so.

receipts.description: Signed records of an eval run. Empty is the correct value until someone actually runs it.

digest.description: The SKILL.md digest this run attests to.

freshness.description: Derived, never authored. live: verified inside stale_after_days. overdue: verification has aged out. dormant: no eval exists but the skill is field-observed. unverified: asserted only.
